summary: Velociti multi-region failover caused inference deadlock, streaming stalls and duplicate completions — post-incident action plan
description:
Issue summary:
Velociti reported a customer-facing outage beginning 2026-03-10 02:12 UTC during an automated multi-region failover test. A subset of routed requests entered a deadlock state in the serving-runtime during fallback routing, leading to streaming stalls, duplicate completions, and elevated token billing for affected customers.

Impact:
- ~42% of Velociti traffic in us-east and eu-west experienced stalled streaming responses for 6–18s before client-side reconnects.
- Duplicate completions were observed in ~4% of affected sessions (identical or near-identical responses returned twice).
- Billing exposure estimated at ~$4.2k for the incident window.
- Customer escalated to enterprise on-call and requested immediate remediation and credits.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-10 02:09 UTC: Canary regional routing change applied (automatic fallback rule updated to prefer quantized variants).
- 2026-03-10 02:12 UTC: Velociti alert (in-app and sent to support) — elevated latencies and streaming stalls.
- 2026-03-10 02:18 UTC: Support triage; SRE paged.
- 2026-03-10 02:24 UTC: Mitigation: rolled back routing change and pinned Velociti traffic to previous model variant.
- 2026-03-10 02:35 UTC: Partial recovery; engineering investigation continues.
- 2026-03-10 05:10 UTC: Full traffic normal for Velociti; incident declared resolved.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Start concurrent multi-region failover simulation targeting fallback to quantized variants with per-tenant fanout >= 12.
2) Inject a routing priority update that triggers simultaneous multipath fanout.
3) Observe serving-runtime streams for stalls and duplicate completions when kernel-selection path flips mid-request.

Logs / Observations:
- Serving-runtime traces show requests stuck at `kv_cache::lock_or_wait` for 8–16s in 1k+ traces.
- Router logs indicate simultaneous re-routing attempts to multiple fallback pools for same session id (multipath fanout).
- Autoscaler metrics showed transient burst that exhausted local GPU pool capacity triggering fallback; concurrent fallback logic attempted routing to two regions in quick succession.
- Trace snippet: https://logs.redwood.com/velociti/2026-03-10/trace-7a12f (SRE-only).

Initial hypothesis:
- Race between multipath fallback routing + KV cache eviction led to lock contention in the runtime when kernel selection changed (quantized -> fp16) mid-stream.
- Router's dedup/affinity window did not sufficiently de-dupe near-simultaneous fallback replays for the same session.

Temporary mitigations applied during incident:
- Rolled back the failing routing rule and pinned Velociti to the pre-change model variant.
- Increased per-tenant concurrency cap for Velociti to avoid autoscaler-induced fallback.
- Disabled cross-region multipath fallback for the customer's tenant until a permanent fix.

Desired outcomes / next steps (post-incident):
- Engineering to develop a runtime fix to abort in-flight kernel flip attempts when KV cache is present (PR referenced below).
- Router changes to enforce stronger de-duplication and an expanded affinity window during failover events.
- Add smoke tests that simulate kernel flip + multipath fallback concurrently.
- Runbook updates: explicitly include steps to pin models and throttle per-tenant concurrency during region failovers.
- Customer-facing: issue apology, provide detailed postmortem, and apply billing credit for measured exposure.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 03:05 UTC — Priya Shah (SRE): found 1.1k traces with >10s waiting on KV lock; correlated with router replay events.
2026-03-10 03:40 UTC — Daniel Ortiz (Runtime Eng): reproduce locally using quantized kernel switch; observed deadlock when cache eviction raced with kernel init.
2026-03-10 04:20 UTC — Marcus Reynolds (Support): temporary mitigation (pinning) reduced customer errors to <1% within 25 minutes.

Hypothesis refinement: kernel switching path lacks checkpointing for in-flight KV references; when cache is reallocated on kernel swap the runtime waits on a lock that the router's replay logic can re-trigger.
Cross-reference: similar symptoms seen in SUP-99555 (GPU pool exhaustion + streaming hang) but root cause differs (here it's kernel flip race).

Priya Shah (SRE) 2026-03-10 02:45 — Identified router multipath replays. Rolling back routing rule now. Will monitor.
Daniel Ortiz (Runtime Eng) 2026-03-10 03:12 — Reproduced deadlock in local harness. Preparing hotfix to short-circuit kernel-change path when KV refs exist.

resolution: Root cause: race condition between router multipath fallback logic and runtime kernel flip path that resulted in lock contention on KV cache during in-flight responses. Fixes applied: (1) rolled back routing change and pinned traffic (mitigation), (2) merged runtime hotfix to abort kernel swap if active KV refs exist (https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1289), (3) router PR to increase dedupe window and serialize fallback for same session (https://github.com/redwood-inference/realtime-router/pull/452). Customer credited $4,200 for exposure and given extended monitoring for 48 hours. Postmortem published to Confluence.
post_incident_actions: ENG-1: Deploy runtime hotfix to canary and run extended quantized kernel flip test (owner: Daniel Ortiz, due: 2026-03-18).
ENG-2: Router dedupe and affinity window change to be rolled out with feature flag (owner: Priya Shah, due: 2026-03-17).
OPS-1: Update failover runbook to include model pinning and per-tenant concurrency throttle during test windows (owner: Marcus Reynolds, due: 2026-03-16).
CS-1: Deliver customer-facing postmortem and confirm acceptance of credit (owner: Elena Park, due: 2026-03-12).
QA-1: Add regression tests to CI that simulate kernel flip + multipath fallback under high fanout (owner: QA Team, due: 2026-03-25).
follow_up_notes: Customer call scheduled 2026-03-11 15:00 UTC (Elena Park, Priya Shah, Daniel Ortiz attending). Will review postmortem, credit details and runbook changes. Engineering to provide canary deployment plan before the call. Flagged for quarterly reliability review. Slack thread: #incidents (https://slack.redwood.com/archives/INC12345).
customer_communication:
03/10/2026 — Initial: Acknowledged incident and provided ETA for mitigation.
03/10/2026 — Update: Routing rollback applied; symptoms reduced.
03/11/2026 — Postmortem: Shared detailed root cause, mitigation steps, and billing credit. Customer accepted credit and requested additional safeguards during planned failovers.
notes_for_postmortem: Include root-cause timeline with kernel flip trace IDs, quantify duplicate completion types (exact dup vs near-duplicate), and runbook gaps that allowed multipath fallback to be enabled during a canary. Recommend policy: disable cross-region multipath during any rolling routing experiments until dedupe improvements land.
customer_impact_summary: Velociti (enterprise) experienced degraded streaming and duplicate completions across US/EU regions for ~3 hours during a scheduled failover; customer traffic returned to normal after rollback and pinning. Billing exposure estimated and credited. Customer is satisfied with remediation but requested guardrails for future failovers.
